content.text:
I fixed it so that the default `maxBodyLength` of `-1` now means unlimited whether or not redirects are followed. I haven't run any tests or tried the issue's reproduction cases against the change.

**Cause:** in `lib/adapters/http.js`, axios only passed `maxBodyLength` to `follow-redirects` when it was greater than `-1`. With the default `-1`, nothing was passed, so `follow-redirects` fell back to its own 10MB limit. That only happens when redirects are followed. With `maxRedirects: 0` the plain Node `http`/`https` modules are used, which have no limit. That's why the issue's cases behaved differently.

**Fix:** when `config.maxBodyLength` is `-1`, axios now passes `Infinity` to `follow-redirects`, so its 10MB default no longer applies. Explicit values are passed through as before. In the issue's examples, the default and `maxBodyLength: -1` cases should now succeed instead of throwing "Request body larger than maxBodyLength limit".

**Docs:** I added one comment line to the `maxBodyLength` entry in `README.md` saying the default is `-1` (unlimited), regardless of `maxRedirects`.

I didn't add a changelog entry for the original 10MB change, which the issue also mentions.
